findings.issue: The header block deviates from the mandated verbatim text. The instruction requires exactly `# Temperature: 0.0`, but the record carries `# Temperature: not sent (claude-opus-5 rejects the parameter; the config's value did not reach the request)`. Header blocks are copied verbatim; replace with `# Temperature: 0.0`.

Plan stated as dataset state via a slot that exists to describe current partitions. The only evidence (NIH RePORTER abstract) is future-tense — 'will provision a holdout test set' — and the value itself says so. A planned split is not a recommended split of the released data; the entry should be removed and, if kept at all, the intention recorded in prose (description/notes), not in `splits`.

Plan stated in a slot for applied methodology. The single entry's own text is future-tense ('will label data with targets important for prediction', 'capabilities are being developed'), i.e. an intended annotation environment rather than a labeling procedure applied to the released data. Remove from `labeling_strategies`.

All three entries push the substantive content into free-text `maintainer_details` while the class's own structure goes unused; `Maintainer` declares `role` and the surrounding prose names distinct people and functions (program manager; two access-request contacts). More importantly these are three distinct entities correctly split, but the contact identity/affiliation content is embedded in prose rather than in declared fields. Where the class offers no name/person field, at minimum the commentary-laden phrasing ('is the contact listed on the CHoRUS project website') should be trimmed to the fact and `role` populated only if the bundle states a role term.

Role mismatch: dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org are given in the GitHub overview under 'Request access', i.e. they are access-request contacts, not stated maintainers of the dataset. This is a value answering a neighboring field; it belongs with `data_governance` (committee/access contact) or `license_and_use_terms.contact_person`, not `maintainers`.

Figure transcription altered from the source unit without flagging it at the value. The website states '1.6 Billion Rows of EHR OMOP data'; the record writes 1600000000, a conversion the source does not print. The `source_caveats` on the entry does disclose the transcription, which mitigates, but the expansion is the record's own computation from a rounded source figure and should be labeled as such (or the rounded figure retained in prose).

Scope conflation: the registration form, licensing agreement and '.edu' email requirement are stated by the cohort 2 webinar as the access route for the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program cohort, not as the general access review process for the CHoRUS dataset. The value should be scoped to the training program or moved/qualified, and the separate GitHub 'Request access' route noted.

`format` values are used to carry data standards/common data models ('OMOP Common Data Model', 'OHNLP open source schema', 'WFDB', 'DICOM', 'EDF+', 'Persyst') rather than distribution file formats. The standards are already correctly recorded in `conforms_to`/`conforms_to_standard` and per-subset `conforms_to`. This duplicates standard information in a slot asking how the dataset is distributed; the bundle states distribution is via a controlled-access cloud enclave, which is a route, not a format — so the slot is better omitted or reduced.

States that documentation is pending rather than answering the field: 'published metadata schemas for clinical notes and for imaging were planned rather than available'. An absence/pending status of documentation is source commentary; it belongs in `source_caveats` or the relevant subset descriptions (where it already appears), not as a dataset limitation entry.

All three entries place content in `external_resources` (a string field on the ExternalResource class) as narrative pointers to where information lives, including the MIT licensing of the software organization. `ExternalResource` also declares `archival`, `restrictions`, `future_guarantees`; none are populated. Entry 3 ('lists www.bridge2ai.org/chorus as a project website') is a pointer to a pointer and adds nothing the bundle attests about the dataset.

Only one Creator entry is emitted although the bundle (cohort 2 webinar) names six CHoRUS leadership team members with affiliations (Eric Rosenthal/MGH; Azra Bihorac, Yulia Strekalova, Parisa Rashidi/University of Florida; Xiaoqian Jiang/UTHealth Houston; Manlik Kwong/Tufts University). The record instead compresses them into `description` prose. Either emit one Creator per named person (without asserting PI status, which the bundle gives only to Rosenthal) or keep them in prose consistently; the current split is an internal inconsistency.

Source commentary is attached at the Creator level explaining why other leadership members are excluded. This is a trust annotation about the roster as a whole and reads better at the record's top-level `source_caveats`; as written it embeds editorial reasoning inside a single person's entry.

Funding amount and project period (5,880,300 USD; 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30) are carried as prose in `notes` on the FundingMechanism. These are bundle-supported facts but the class declares no field for them, so `notes` is defensible; flagging only that the award amount is an attribute of the award rather than of the dataset and risks being read as dataset budget.

The single entry answers nothing the slot asks for: it states only that collection is retrospective (already captured in `acquisition_methods`) and then records, in `source_caveats`, that the calendar range is unknown. No `start_date`/`end_date` is supportable. A timeframe entry with no timeframe is an absence dressed as a value; omit the slot and keep the retrospective character in `acquisition_methods`.

`is_direct: false` is an inference, and the entry's own `source_caveats` admits 'No source states the direct or indirect character of collection in those terms'. A boolean the bundle does not state should be omitted; the extraction-from-systems description can stand in `acquisition_methods`.

Nine subset fragment labels are minted on the record's own id (https://chorus4ai.org/), which is a project/site root rather than a dataset-specific identifier. This is permitted (it is the identifier the record carries in `id` and `page`), but no value elsewhere in the record points at any of these fragments, so under the fragment rule these parts are described rather than referenced. `DataSubset` requires `id`, so the ids must stay if the entries stay; note only that the labels carry no cross-reference.

Three entries set `subpopulation_elements_present: true` and give only an `identification` string; `distribution` is unpopulated although the bundle gives no per-unit counts. The entries are supported only by the phrase '50,000 Patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU', which attests that the three unit types are covered, not that they constitute documented subpopulations with representation figures. Acceptable but thin.

The keyword list is drawn from the NIH RePORTER 'Preferred terms' line, which is the correct provenance for `keywords`. Mixed capitalization is inherited from the source ('acute care', 'data acquisition' lowercase alongside 'Critical Care'); harmless but inconsistent within one list.

`tools` takes the single value 'OHNLP toolkit' with no `tool_accuracy`; supported. Note only that the OHNLP toolkit is used for extraction/tokenization of notes, which the record also records under `preprocessing_strategies` and `collection_mechanisms` — the same fact appears in three slots, which risks reading as three distinct activities.

Omitted although the bundle supports a determination indirectly (clinical notes retained locally; de-identification 'in process' for imaging implies identifiable content in the un-de-identified imaging cohort). Because no source states the presence of identifiable elements in the released data outright, omission is the safer reading; flagged as a possible supported omission only.

Clearly supported omission candidates are absent: the bundle describes community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, patient-focused legal and ethical work on privacy and bias, and a consortium ethics pillar. No IRB approval, consent mechanism or ethics committee is named for the dataset itself, so omitting `ethical_reviews`, `collection_consents` and `human_subject_research` is defensible; however the ethics focus-group activity is bundle-supported and currently appears nowhere in the record.

Omitted. The bundle states CHoRUS is one of four data generation projects in the Bridge2AI consortium and that it collaborates with the other three, but it does not state a typed relationship to any named dataset, and `DatasetRelationship` requires both `relationship_type` and `target_dataset`. Omission is correct; recorded for completeness of the audit.

The website banner quotation is residual content and correctly placed, but it is a statement about the website's administrative review status, not about the dataset. Retaining it is acceptable under `notes`; it should not be read as a dataset status.

summary: Twenty-three findings against the full record. Two high-severity items require repair before the record can be considered conformant: the header `# Temperature:` line deviates from the mandated verbatim text, and `splits` plus `labeling_strategies` each state a future-tense plan (a holdout test set that 'will' be provisioned; an annotation environment that 'will' label data) as the dataset's current state — both entries admit their own future tense and should be removed from those slots. Medium findings cluster around slot-fit rather than evidence: `distribution_formats` carries data standards already recorded in `conforms_to`/`conforms_to_standard` rather than distribution formats, `data_governance.access_review_process` describes the AIM-AHEAD training-program access route as though it were the general process, two `maintainers` entries are in fact access-request contacts belonging with governance or license terms, one `known_limitations` entry reports that metadata documentation is pending rather than stating a limitation of the data, and the 1.6 Billion-to-1600000000 expansion is the record's own conversion of a rounded source figure (disclosed in an entry caveat, which mitigates). Low findings concern thin or inferential entries — a `collection_timeframes` entry containing no timeframe, a `direct_collection` boolean the record's own caveat says no source states, a single Creator where the bundle names six leadership members whom the record otherwise lists only in `description` — and note bundle-supported material that appears nowhere in the record, chiefly the community-facing ethics focus groups. Evidence grounding is otherwise sound: the two admission-count figures (50,000 website vs. over 45K webinar) and the divergent imaging units are disclosed in top-level `source_caveats` with the higher-ranked source preferred, the misspelled program-manager address is transcribed as printed and flagged, and the MIT License is correctly attributed to the software organization rather than to the dataset.
